title: Allowances
subject: Visigoth Bank, an invented retail bank

records.title: Set an allowance
Enforce at purchase
Tell the card user
Tell the cardholder
Service and comply
Cardholder sets a monthly amount per card user
records.statement: The cardholder can set one monthly spending amount for each authorized card user on the account.
acceptance: Amount can be set from $10 to the card's credit limit
Each card user has their own amount
A card user with no amount set is unaffected

records.title: Store a limit for each card user
records.summary: The limits API already holds a per-card limit. Each card user has their own card number, so no new storage is needed.

evidence.quote: Limits can be set per card and take effect on the next authorization.

records.title: Card limits API
records.summary: Holds a spend limit per card and is read at approval time.
records.gaps: None found.

records.title: Customer profile attributes
records.summary: Could hold the amount as a profile attribute.
records.gaps: Not readable at approval time, so it cannot enforce anything.

records.title: Allowance resets on a day the cardholder picks
records.statement: The allowance returns to its full amount on a day of the month chosen by the cardholder.
acceptance: Any day from the 1st to the 28th can be chosen
The reset happens at midnight in the account's time zone

records.title: Reset the allowance on a chosen day
records.summary: A scheduled job can reset each limit on its chosen day. The limits API's own reset only works on calendar months.

evidence.quote: Jobs can be scheduled per account with a day-of-month rule.

records.title: Scheduled jobs platform
records.summary: Runs a job per account on any day of the month.
records.gaps: Needs a retry rule for failed resets.

records.title: Card limits API
records.summary: Has a built-in monthly reset.
records.gaps: Calendar month only; no chosen day.

records.title: A changed amount takes effect right away
records.statement: When the cardholder raises or lowers the amount mid-cycle, the new amount applies to the next purchase.
acceptance: A change applies within 5 minutes
Spend so far in the cycle still counts

records.title: Apply a changed limit immediately
records.summary: A limit change through the API reaches approvals within about five minutes.

records.title: Card limits API
records.summary: Limit updates propagate to the approval path.
records.gaps: Up to 5 minutes of delay, which meets the acceptance line but not 'right away'.

records.title: One allowance per card user, not per merchant type
records.statement: At launch there is a single allowance per card user. Category budgets are out of scope.
acceptance: No category controls appear in the app
records.explore_note: No platform dependency. This is a product rule, enforced by leaving category controls out of the design.

records.title: Purchases approved live are declined past the limit
records.statement: A purchase that is approved in real time is declined when it would take the card user over the allowance.
acceptance: A purchase equal to the remaining amount is approved
A purchase one cent over is declined

records.title: Decline at approval when over the limit
records.summary: A rule in the authorization engine can compare the purchase with the remaining limit.

evidence.quote: Rules evaluate in the approval path and can return a decline reason.

records.title: Authorization rules engine
records.summary: Rules can read the card's limit and decline with a chosen reason.
records.gaps: None found.

records.title: Card limits API
records.summary: The limits API has a hard-limit flag that declines by itself.
records.gaps: Uses a generic reason code, which conflicts with R-08.

records.title: Charges that skip live approval are counted, not blocked
records.statement: Charges that post without live approval, such as transit taps, count toward the allowance but are not stopped.
acceptance: Such charges reduce the remaining amount when they post
The cardholder is told when they push spend past the allowance
records.explore_question: Counting charges that skip live approval relies on the spend events stream, which can lag by up to 2 hours. Is a 2-hour delay acceptable at launch, or should this wait for stand-in processing settings, which has no release date?

records.title: Count charges that skip live approval
records.summary: Posted charges appear on the spend events stream and can be subtracted from the allowance after the fact.

evidence.quote: Posting events are delivered within 2 hours of posting.
Stand-in processing settings: planned, not yet scheduled.

records.title: Spend events stream
records.summary: Every posted charge is published with its card and amount.
records.gaps: Lags by up to 2 hours.

records.title: Stand-in processing settings
records.summary: Would let the processor apply the limit even when approval is offline.
records.gaps: Planned, with no release date.

records.title: Refunds return to the allowance in the same cycle
records.statement: A refund received in the same cycle as the purchase adds back to the remaining allowance.
acceptance: A refund in a later cycle does not change that cycle's allowance

records.title: Return refunds to the allowance
records.summary: Refunds appear on the same stream as purchases and can be matched to the original cycle.

records.title: Spend events stream
records.summary: Refund events carry the original purchase reference.
records.gaps: Matching to a cycle is our logic to build.

records.title: Authorization rules engine
records.summary: A rule could adjust the limit on refund authorizations.
records.gaps: Most refunds are not authorized in real time.

records.title: A limit decline carries its own reason code
records.statement: Declines caused by the allowance are distinguishable from every other kind of decline.
acceptance: The app and the agent desktop can both read the reason

records.title: A reason code for limit declines
records.summary: The catalog accepts new reason codes and both the app and the agent desktop read from it.

evidence.quote: Reason codes are configurable and exposed to channels.

records.title: Decline reason catalog
records.summary: New codes can be added with a display text.
records.gaps: A code takes one release cycle to appear.

records.title: The limit check adds under 50 ms to approval
records.statement: Checking the allowance must not noticeably slow a purchase.
acceptance: Added time is under 50 ms at the 99th percentile
Measured at twice the expected peak volume

records.title: Card user sees what is left before paying
records.statement: The card user can see the remaining allowance and the reset date in the app.
acceptance: The amount shown is no more than 1 minute old
The reset date is shown beside it

records.title: Show the remaining allowance in the app
records.summary: The account controls module can host a new card for the allowance.

records.title: Account controls module
records.summary: Has a slot for per-card controls and balances.
records.gaps: Design work needed for the card user's view.

records.title: Read the remaining amount in near real time
records.summary: The limits API returns the amount left on request.

evidence.quote: GET limit returns used and remaining.

records.title: Card limits API
records.summary: Returns limit and amount used for a card.
records.gaps: Does not include charges that are counted later (see R-06).

records.title: Spend events stream
records.summary: Could total spend from events.
records.gaps: Too slow for a one-minute freshness target.

records.title: Card user is told why a purchase was declined
records.statement: After a limit decline the card user gets a message that names the allowance as the reason.
acceptance: The message arrives within 10 seconds
It shows how far over the purchase was

records.title: Tell the card user why a purchase was declined
records.summary: A decline with the new reason code can trigger a push message.

evidence.quote: Push supports event-triggered templates with amounts.

records.title: Push notification service
records.summary: Sends a templated message on a decline event.
records.gaps: Needs the reason code from R-08 first.

records.title: Account controls module
records.summary: Could show the reason in the app's activity list.
records.gaps: Not immediate; the user must open the app.

records.title: Card user can ask for a top-up
records.statement: The card user can request more allowance for the current cycle from the decline message or the app.
acceptance: A request names an amount and an optional note
Only one request can be open at a time
records.explore_question: The request and approve service fits well but is in beta with no support commitment. Accept that for launch, or build a simpler request inside the app?

records.title: A top-up request flow
records.summary: A request-and-approve pattern exists as a shared service.

evidence.quote: Request and approve service: beta, best-effort support.

records.title: Request and approve service
records.summary: Handles a request, a notification to an approver and the answer.
records.gaps: Beta. No support commitment.

records.title: Account controls module
records.summary: Build a request screen and store requests ourselves.
records.gaps: New storage and notifications to build.

records.title: Running-low alert at a threshold the cardholder sets
records.statement: The card user is alerted when the remaining allowance falls below a threshold.
acceptance: Threshold can be an amount or a percentage

records.title: Cardholder approves or declines a top-up request
records.statement: The cardholder can answer a top-up request in one step from a notification.
acceptance: Approval raises this cycle's allowance only
The card user is told the outcome

records.title: Statement shows spend by card user
records.statement: The monthly statement groups spend by card user and shows each allowance.
acceptance: Each card user has a subtotal
The allowance amount appears beside the subtotal

records.title: Spend by card user on the statement
records.summary: The statement composer can group lines, but template changes are slow to ship.

evidence.quote: Template changes ship on a two-cycle lead time.

records.title: Statement composer
records.summary: Supports grouping lines by card.
records.gaps: A template change takes two statement cycles to go live.

records.title: Spend events stream
records.summary: Show the same breakdown in the app from spend events.
records.gaps: Does not change the paper or PDF statement.

records.title: Cardholder is alerted when counted charges exceed the allowance
records.statement: When charges that were counted but not blocked take a card user past the allowance, the cardholder is alerted.
acceptance: One alert per cycle per card user
The alert names the merchant of the charge

records.title: Agents can see a card user's allowance and recent declines
records.statement: Servicing agents can see the allowance, the remaining amount and limit declines for any card user.
acceptance: Shown in the existing account view
Declines list covers 90 days

records.title: Agent view of allowance and declines
records.summary: The account panel can add a section fed by the limits API and the decline catalog.

evidence.quote: Account panel sections are configured, not coded.

records.title: Agent desktop account panel
records.summary: Panels are configurable per product.
records.gaps: Needs a 90-day decline query that does not exist yet.

records.title: A limit decline is never scored as fraud
records.statement: Declines caused by the allowance must not raise the card's fraud score or trigger a block.
acceptance: No fraud case is opened for a limit decline

records.title: Keep limit declines out of fraud scoring
records.summary: The exclusions list can ignore a named reason code.

evidence.quote: Exclusions are keyed by decline reason.

records.title: Fraud rule exclusions
records.summary: Excludes declines by reason code from scoring.
records.gaps: Depends on the new code from R-08.

records.title: Disclosure explains what the limit covers
records.statement: Cardholders are told, before turning the feature on, which charges are blocked and which are only counted.
acceptance: Wording is approved by Compliance
Shown once at setup and available later

records.title: Card users under 18 need recorded consent
records.statement: An allowance for a card user under 18 requires the cardholder's recorded consent.
acceptance: Consent is stored with a date
Feature cannot be turned on without it
